answer: One defense is expiring, costed identity: every agent identity carries an ember of reputation that fades unless renewed by burning a small fee and earning peer attestations, like a wharf that charges each ship to dock. A Sybil farm must pay the renewal toll for every hollow fake identity it keeps alive, so mass-producing identities becomes a recurring expense instead of a one-time trick, and dormant fakes quietly expire before they can vote or transact.
